queries: The PKC gene and its upstream promoter region were amplified as a single contiguous fragment from genomic DNA of the citrus fungal pathogen. The full-length amplicon spanned the promoter, the complete open reading frame, and a short downstream terminator sequence, yielding a product of several kilobases in size. To assess the functional role of PKC in pathogenicity, a series of truncated constructs were generated by deleting specific domains or promoter elements. These included a construct lacking the N-terminal regulatory domain, a construct with a partial promoter deletion that removed putative binding sites for transcription factors, and a construct retaining only the catalytic kinase domain under the native promoter. Each truncated version was introduced into a PKC deletion mutant via transformation, and restoration of pathogenicity was evaluated on citrus leaves or fruits. Only the full-length construct fully restored wild-type virulence, while the truncated variants showed partial or no complementation, indicating that both the promoter integrity and the complete coding sequence are essential for proper PKC function during infection. The results highlight the importance of PKC in regulating downstream signaling pathways required for host colonization and lesion formation.

candidates.text: The primer pair CXAC1230.F/CXAC1230.R was used to amplify a 1447 bp DNA fragment that contained the PKC gene and its promoter region. The PCR product was cloned into the vector pBBR1MCS-5 to obtain the construct pBB-XAC1230. The pBB-XAC1230 construct was transformed into the deletion mutant for complementation analysis. Complementation with the PKC mutants was additionally studied by designing specific primers to combine with CXAC1230.F to generate constructs expressing 1–100, 1–180, and 1–255 amino acids of the PKC protein. The corresponding generated constructs M1-255, M1-180, and M1-100 were transformed into the deletion mutant to evaluate their ability to restore pathogenicity.

The primer pair CXAC1230.F/CXAC1230.R was used to amplify a 1447 bp DNA fragment that contained the PKC gene and its promoter region. The PCR product was cloned into the vector pBBR1MCS-5 to obtain the construct pBB-XAC1230. The pBB-XAC1230 construct was transformed into the deletion mutant for complementation analysis. Complementation with the PKC mutants was additionally studied by designing specific primers to combine with CXAC1230.F to generate constructs expressing 1–100, 1–180, and 1–255 amino acids of the PKC protein. The corresponding generated constructs M1-255, M1-180, and M1-100 were transformed into the deletion mutant to evaluate their ability to restore pathogenicity.

Since the first complete genome sequence of X. citri subsp. citri was released, numerous multiple studies have reported the virulence genes from this pathogen based on a genome-wide analysis. The necessity of PKC for citrus canker development was determined in both X. citri subsp. citri 306 and 29–1 strains using Tn5-based random mutagenesis. In this study, a non-polar deletion mutant of the PKC gene was created to verify its necessity for virulence in hosts and induction of the HR in nonhost plants. Based on a sequence analysis, the conserved SRPBCC and GyrI binding-domains were evaluated for their contribution for virulence. In addition, the levels of expression of the type III genes and changes in the biosynthesis of metabolites were studied in the deletion mutant, thus, significantly advancing the current understanding of the role of PKC.
